findings.summary: The firm describes itself as a public-system, multiemployer and life-insurer practice, but none of its six engagements is for a public system or a multiemployer fund, and four are private single-employer corporate work that no overview lists as a service.
findings.evidence: d:0054 (2022 overview): "Our clients are the boards, trustees and officers who answer for long-term obligations: pensions owed to public employees and to the members of multiemployer funds, and the reserves a life insurer holds", then cites Howard and Sons, Miller, Cook and Snyder, Estes Group and Martinez LLC "as examples of the kinds of organizations we work for" (d:0040 does the same for the first two). Those clients are corporate plan sponsors: d:0002 "the pension plan that Howard and Sons sponsors for its employees ... the largest contribution the company may deduct"; d:0030 "the Estes Group retirement plan still describe your workforce", with questions about layoffs and business units sold; d:0044 "the company's financial reporting under ASC Topic 715"; d:0056 "the company's pension plan ... PBGC premiums". A public plan has no deduction limit, reports under GASB rather than ASC 715, and pays no PBGC premiums. The services the overviews list (GASB 67/68 reports, PPA zone certification, rehabilitation plans; d:0009, d:0040) appear in no engagement folder, and the corporate funding and ASC 715 work that fills the folders appears in no overview.

findings.summary: Who writes which engagement document runs against seniority: after 2016, associates and analysts issue the kickoff memos and client status reports that assign work to the lead actuary, while the Managing Actuary takes the minutes at every session he attends.
findings.evidence: Five of six kickoff memos and five of six status reports come from someone junior to the engagement lead. d:0057 is addressed "To: Robert Lawrence, David Sherman / From: Michelle Banks" (an Actuarial Associate under three years in) and tells its readers to "note it and pass it to Robert Lawrence rather than taking it on within the study", that is, to pass it to one of the memo's own two recipients. d:0017 has Megan Dudley, Actuarial Associate, setting out that her supervisor "Jennifer Vasquez leads the review day to day and will take the assumption work herself". The client status reports are headed "Prepared by Karen Harris, Actuarial Associate, with Michelle Banks and Robert Lawrence" (d:0072), "Prepared by Michelle Banks, with David Sherman and Robert Lawrence" (d:0060), and "by Megan Dudley, with Jennifer Vasquez and David Sherman" (d:0025). Meanwhile the minutes of all three sessions Lawrence attends are his own, with associates in the room: d:0059 "Robert Lawrence prepared them" (Michelle Banks present), and d:0037 and d:0071 are likewise authored by him.

findings.summary: Linda Hanna's onboarding record presents the Practice Manager role as newly needed, although Carol Cooper held that title and those duties from 2014 until five weeks before Hanna started, and no document mentions Cooper leaving or Hanna replacing her.
findings.evidence: d:0042 (January 2020): "The practice has reached the size where engagement paperwork, billing and the tracking of client files need one person who owns them. Linda is that person." Compare d:0009 (2016): "Carol Cooper, our Practice Manager, runs the practice day to day. She prepares engagement letters, keeps the schedule, sends and tracks data requests, and looks after invoicing and the retention of our files." d:0003 also assigns Cooper the billing code, transfer site and request log. An eight-person firm's record for a replacement hire would say whom she replaced.

findings.summary: The client side does not look like the people who commission actuarial work: five of six counterparts are operations generalists, and the two insurance clients carry names in the style of law partnerships.
findings.evidence: The pension sponsor's contact is "Elizabeth Horne, Director of Operations" (d:0002), and d:0012 asks her to decide the mortality basis. The ASC 715 client's contact is "Jason Wagner, General Manager" (d:0044), who selects the discount rate. The reserve-opinion client's contact is "Michelle Hudson, Director of Operations" (d:0016). The other two are Chief Operating Officers. The correspondence keeps sending the real questions to unnamed "benefits staff" (d:0005), "HR staff" (d:0034) and "finance team" (d:0066), and no benefits manager, plan administrator, controller or client actuary appears anywhere. The insurer that cedes a life block to "its reinsurers" is "Gonzalez, Campbell and Kelly" (d:0064), and the one that carries reserves for an opinion is "Miller, Cook and Snyder" (d:0016). Both read as law-firm names, not insurer names.

findings.summary: The firm works out of one office suite, but its staff's email signatures carry phone numbers in five metro area codes, which suggests a multi-office firm.
findings.evidence: One Howard and Sons thread is signed "Jennifer Vasquez / Consulting Actuary / +1 (206) 555-0123" (Seattle) and "Jeffrey Ochoa / Actuarial Analyst / +1 (303) 555-0117" (Denver). The office-logistics mail about the large conference room closing (d:0015) is signed "David Sherman / Senior Analyst / +1 (312) 555-0179" (Chicago). Robert Lawrence signs from +1 (212) and Michelle Banks from +1 (415). Yet d:0051 describes a single building with "the lobby turnstiles and ... the door to our suite", and no document mentions a second office. Mobile numbers could explain a few of these, but not a spread across five cities.

findings.summary: No firm overview ever names Jennifer Vasquez, the firm's only other actuary and every client's day-to-day contact, and the 2016 overview introduces the Practice Manager in her place, so the firm reads as a two-person shop.
findings.evidence: d:0009 (May 2016), under "Who you will work with", names only Robert Lawrence and "Carol Cooper, our Practice Manager", then says the firm intends "to add people on the consulting side first". The roster at that date already held a Consulting Actuary, a Senior Analyst, an Actuarial Analyst and an Actuarial Associate. A month earlier, d:0002 told the client "Most of the time you will hear from Jennifer Vasquez." d:0054 (2022) refers only to unnamed "Our consulting actuaries" (the firm has one) beside the named Managing Actuary.
